Chief Executive’s Foreword 
 
A major milestone in the MetroLink project was reached this 
month with the publication of the Railway Order by An 
Coimisiún Pleanála. Planning for the arrival of MetroLink by 
Fingal County Council has been proceeding for several years 
now and we are very pleased that the project will now 
advance with the granting of the planning permission. The 
route will take passengers directly from Swords to Dublin City 
in 25 minutes and will provide service users with a fast, 
efficient and sustainable service with trains every three 
minutes. The benefits for the people of Fingal, and further 
afield, will be immense as the service will be capable of 
accommodating up to 20,000 passengers per hour in each 
direction therefore easing traffic congestion and providing 
commuters with more transport choices to link with Dublin 
Airport, DART, rail and bus services and to the city. 
Economically, the project will mean the enacting of Master 
Plans 
to 
develop 
housing 
and 
explore 
economic 
opportunities along the route.  MetroLink will be 18.8km long 
and will run from Swords to Charlemont with 16 stations, 
seven of them in Fingal. The Fingal stations will be Estuary, 
Seatown, Swords Central, Fosterstown, Dublin Airport, 
Dardistown and Northwood. Fingal County Council welcomes 
the news of the advancement of the project and we look 
forward to continuing the good working relationship with 
MetroLink as well as with all other stakeholders on the next 
phase of the works. 
Enhancing Fingal County Council’s online experience for our 
customers has been a focus as part of an overall 
transformation of digital services. 90% of local authority 
services will be available online by 2030 and will 
fundamentally change how people interact with their council. 
The latest improvement will give council tenants the flexibility 
to pay their rents online. This option will give our customers 
access to manage their rent accounts 24/7 as well as 
providing those who face challenges when accessing in 
person services with a more efficient way to make their 
payments. Of course, the existing methods of payment 
remain the same - Council cash offices will continue to accept 
in-person payments (cash, cheque, card) and payments over 
the phone. Tenants can also use a Rent Card, available upon 
request, to pay at An Post offices and BillPay retailers. 
Standing orders and the Household Budget scheme remain 
active payment options. To access the system, go to 
www.fingal.ie/council/service/rent-payment 
and 
follow 
instructions. Users need their Rent Account number and 
email address; they can pay rent, view charges, and clear any 
arrears. I hope that our customers find this to be an efficient 
and user-friendly means to manage their household 
finances. 
I was delighted to have joined Mayor of Fingal, Cllr Tom 
O’Leary, representatives from Fingal County Council’s Parks 
and Landscapes division and Meakstown Community Group 
in Meakstown recently for the official opening of the 
community garden.  
Located adjacent to the Community Centre and 
children’s playground, in the heart of the locality, the 
garden is a visual and sensory masterpiece for visitors 
and locals to enjoy. Designed by award-winning 
designer, Jane McCorkell, the garden is divided into 
three spaces containing urban elements, a forest bath, 
and simple landscape features. The layout and chosen 
plants and ornamental grasses really encourage and 
entice visitors to explore the garden and discover its 
sensory properties. All the materials that were used in 
the creation of the garden have come from council 
depots and demonstrate what can be achieved when 
you reduce, reuse and recycle. I wish to thank the 
Parks 
and 
Landscapes 
teams 
who 
worked 
collaboratively with Meakstown Community Group to 
see this project to fruition. Gardens are spaces for 
socialising, taking time for quiet reflection and to truly 
see biodiversity in action. I have no doubt that this 
beautiful space will be a much-loved amenity in 
Meakstown for the future. 
With the weeks advancing and plans for trick or 
treating already beginning, it’s a sure sign that 
Halloween is just around the corner! In Fingal, we have 
a proud tradition of celebrating Halloween with the 
fantastic Festival of Fire events comprising of a spooky 
themed live DJ followed by spectacular fireworks 
displays. This year, to enhance the Halloween 
celebrations, we are delighted to be chosen as a hub 
for ‘Ireland, Home of Halloween’ – The strategy, which 
was developed collaboratively by Fáilte Ireland, 
Tourism Ireland, and Tourism Northern Ireland, seeks 
to create a link with our Halloween festivities and our 
ancient history and culture and the marking of 
Samhain, which traditionally meant the end of the 
harvest season and the beginning of winter. The 
Wonderful 
family 
friendly 
events 
planned 
will 
complement 
the 
already 
stellar 
Halloween 
programme we have in place and will ensure 
enjoyment for all not just on Halloween night itself but 
throughout the month of October. Many of the events 
in our Libraries, Arts Centres and historic castles are 
free to enter and to whet your appetite, here is a 
snapshot of just some of the events on offer: 
Pumpkins After Dark in Newbridge House & Farm, 
Harvest Food Fair in the Séamus Ennis Arts Centre, Flip 
Animation Workshop in the Dráiocht Theatre, A 
Traitorous Tale in Malahide Castle & Gardens and 
Skerries Mills Family Fireshow Spectacular. All these 
and 
many 
more 
events 
are 
listed 
on 
www.fingal.ie/halloween I would encourage everyone 
to take the opportunity to visit some of these events 
as we celebrate the Samhain season - I’m sure a 
wonderful experience awaits you all.  
AnnMarie Farrelly 
Chief Executive

Swords Castle  
The objectives of the Swords Castle conservation 
plan, include the aim of making as many 
enriching experiences and memories of Swords 
Castle for the local people as possible.  
 
The local 49th Scouts Troop a.k.a. Swords Scouts 
camped inside the range in September. Over 120 
youth members - from Beaver Scouts to Rover 
Scouts - enjoyed a medieval themed camp filled 
with fun activities, in the local historical 
landmark. This included orienteering, campfires, 
songs and camaraderie. 
 
Feedback from the well behaved and polite 
young members focussed on how exciting it was 
to spend a night at the Castle.

the county’s rich cultural landscape. This annual 
national event invited audiences of all ages to 
experience an exciting evening of creativity, 
heritage, culture, and community. Key highlights 
included a special event at County Hall, Swords, 
marking Fingal County Council’s vision for 
Culture House, part of the upcoming Swords 
Cultural 
Quarter. 
The 
evening 
featured 
performances by the Forget Me Nots Choir, as

Declan Brady.

Swords 
Castle 
and 
the 
Carnegie 
Library,

offered family-friendly events at branches in

Theatre, Cinema & Comedy   
 
The month kicked off with a raucous evening of 
storytelling with Clare Murphy and her new 
show, The Spanking 
Goddess and Other 
Discarded Tales (sold out – 90 attendees). 
Following this was a Talk entitled, ‘Is Bob Dylan 
now History? An Evening with Michael Gray.’ 
Gray is the pioneer of Dylan studies and the talk 
asked the question, ‘Now that we’re a quarter 
through the 21st century, can Dylan be anything

Regarding the 30kph in built up & urban 
areas, the Department of Transport originally 
communicated that there would be a default 
speed limit of 30kph set for these.   This was 
changed  as there is no definition of urban 
areas in legislation with regards to the setting 
of speed limits.  In order to implement a 
default 30kph in urban areas, there would 
need to be updated legislation which would 
take some time.  Therefore the Department 
of Transport communicated to Councils that 
we were to proceed with the review and 
implementation of urban speed limits by 
special speed limit bye-laws rather than a 
change in the default speed limit.  In order to 
undertake the process of setting special 
speed limits in built up & urban areas, the 
Guidelines for Setting and Managing Speed 
Limits in Ireland are being revised.  They have 
not yet been issued to us.  The best 
timeframe we have is that they will be issued 
in Q3 2025 via a new Circular.  The circular 
will direct the LA’s to commence the process 
of reviewing speed limits in our areas and to 
set speed limits in accordance with the new 
Guidelines.

Design studies and a preliminary design to 
encapsulate the existing pier and construct a 
new, larger pier around it were completed in 
2024. Planning Approval for the proposal was 
granted by An Bord Pleanála on 4th 
September 2024.

Foreshore Licences to the Department of 
Agriculture, Food & Marine (DAFM) in 
December 2024. Two such licences were 
applied for:- (a) to undertake boreholes in 
the seabed so as to inform the engineering 
design of the foundations required for the 
new pier. This would allow the engineering 
design to be completed, and tenders issued 
to the market to procure contractors for the 
construction of the new pier, AND (b) a 
licence to carry out the construction of the

progressed by DAFM but may take up to 18 
months meaning it could be 2027/8 before

increases the risk of a sudden collapse of the 
pier.

Fingal County Council’s Affordable & Cost Rental

below market rent. 
What is Cost Rental? 
Cost Rental housing is designed to provide 
affordable rental homes for people who are above 
the social housing income limits but still struggle to 
afford market rents. Rent is based on the cost of 
building, managing, and maintaining the homes – 
not market rates. 
Who Can Apply? 
To be eligible for Cost Rental housing, applicants 
must: 
• 
Be aged 18 years or over 
• 
Have a net household income of €66,000 
or less per annum 
• 
Not be in receipt of social housing 
supports (including HAP or RAS) 
• 
Not own or have a legal interest in a 
property 
• 
Be able to afford the rent and comply with 
the terms of the tenancy
